study.question: Can adding detached content after the scalar ReLU recover incremental content-freshness utility while retaining count/freshness evidence, compared with injecting the identical content before that ReLU?
study.hypothesis: Observed: exclusive-second incumbent AUC 0.620342615 exceeds all round-13 content variants. Detaching the direct content embedding gradient raises covariance AUC from 0.619757734 to 0.620170239 and marginal-product AUC from 0.619352759 to 0.619715614, but neither exceeds incumbent. Source inspection: content is still added before the same ReLU that reads scalar evidence. Provisional mechanism: shared threshold crossings suppress useful scalar activations and clip signed covariance increments. Replacing relu(z+p) by relu(z)+p may preserve the scalar activation support and expose signed content. This does not freeze learned scalar weights, remove all gradient interference, or establish the cause of prior degradation.

nearest_work.difference: Same content summaries, detach boundary, allocation, gate and output weights. Only content injection moves from before to after scalar ReLU. Shared covariance replays the prior training graph.
Reuses marginal-product content E[v]E[d] as matched-dimensional content replacement; it is invariant to within-cell age reassignment, whereas covariance E[vd]-E[v]E[d] is not.

DIN uses target-conditioned weighted history pooling and explicitly preserves interest intensity. We inherit the field embeddings and target-aware baseline lineage but use existing semantic means plus explicit statistics; the new change is a local readout bypass, not DIN reproduction.

External FM Highway bypasses a residual stack with per-layer dot products. We test a related direct-route principle through one scalar ReLU using existing covariance or marginal-product summaries and shared output/gate; no tokens, FM dot products, two buses, auxiliary labels or source recipe. Tiny-mode removal evidence does not prove local transfer or novelty.

inherited_components: Frozen causal prefix limited to 128 events, full first-six-day training exposures, natural prevalence, three epochs, batch 4096, seed 42, host optimizer/loss/scorer and split.
All round-14 module allocations and order, 16-dimensional embeddings, hidden widths [128,64], dormant attention, four target-match pools, total count statistics.
Exclusive action-by-match count, one-day mean decay and second moment; multiplicative RMS-normalized context gate and scalar correction.

All four temporal content summaries computed; direct content embedding gradient detached, while inherited pools, gate and base gradients remain active. Content projection 256->32 zero-initialized after all incumbent modules.
study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 content-signal x readout factorial. Let z=W_s[count,mean]+W_m second and p=W_c stopgrad(content). shared: h=ReLU(z+p); bypass: h=ReLU(z)+p. Both use the same w^T[h*(1+tanh(RMS(W_g context)))] plus backbone logit. No new parameters or learned head. Both hidden forms computed in all variants; only selected route contributes gradients. Covariance=E[vd]-E[v]E[d] versus marginal product=E[v]E[d]. Zero p gives identical scalar forward function; initial p=0 and correction output weights=0 preserve ancestor initial logits. This is a new local mechanism contrast, not a verified novelty claim.
predictions: Primary: bypass_covariance exceeds shared_covariance on full validation AUC and exceeds incumbent 0.620342615 if retained content provides practical incremental utility. Report Logloss separately.

Content attribution: covariance exceeds factorized under bypass; examine (bypass_covariance-shared_covariance)-(bypass_factorized-shared_factorized). A route gain for both signals supports a generic readout effect rather than covariance-specific complementarity.

Diagnostics: bypass identity h-ReLU(z)=p holds to floating tolerance; zero-content route identity holds. Shared threshold-crossing fraction and readout gap can be nonzero at trained checkpoint. These are label-free activation observations, not causal evidence of predictive benefit.

Within-cell age swaps preserve counts, means, second moments, uniform content and factorized content; covariance and its logits can change. Empty, zero-length, padding and permutation behavior remains valid. Diagnostics are first-512 candidate measurements only.
falsifiers: If bypass covariance does not improve shared covariance, the proposed readout remedy lacks local support at the frozen recipe; do not refute every possible content mechanism.
If bypass covariance fails to exceed the stronger incumbent, practical additional utility remains unsupported even if the route contrast improves.
If only marginal-product content improves, or covariance advantage disappears under paired repetitions, covariance-specific benefit remains unsupported.
Failed finite outputs, nonzero empty correction, broken masking/algebra or unexpectedly different allocations invalidate the comparison before interpreting AUC.
Shared control divergence from round-14 source beyond execution tolerance requires investigating source/runtime differences; replay is never counted as an independent seed.
alternative_explanations: Bypass changes the function class and direct gradient flow: it removes nonlinear scalar-content interaction and acts as a simpler regularized content reader. Equal parameter count does not equal effective capacity.
Shared output weights and context gate remain jointly learned, so bypass does not isolate every source of optimization interference and scalar parameters can still drift.
Covariance and factorized signals have different scales, sparsity and information; positive contrast does not uniquely identify content-age binding as the causal source.

Single-seed selection across many validation-guided rounds may produce chance gains. Slice changes are exploratory, repeated exposures are user-correlated, and numerical replays add no independent evidence.
The sparse fields, capped history, undocumented static-snapshot as-of dates and frozen three-epoch recipe limit conclusions; coarser history might lack meaningful residual content information.
